newsitem.title: JAPAN: World commodity prices to rise in 1997 -- Marubeni.
newsitem.headline: World commodity prices to rise in 1997 -- Marubeni.

text.p: Marubeni Corp said on Friday it expects global commodity prices, led by soybeans, to resume their upward trend at the beginning of next year, buoyed in large part by economic growth in Asia.
The giant trade house said in a report that soybeans in particular are likely to garner the spotlight in commodity markets, reflecting expected heavy imports by China and low U.S. inventories.
"Prices of nearby soybean futures in the Chicago market could climb to $10 per bushel, depending on weather conditions," the report said.
The trade house said price gains in corn are likely to be hampered by a bumper wheat harvest in the 1996/97 crop year, with feed markers increasingly shifting to wheat from corn.
Chicago soybean futures have recently traded around $7 a bushel and corn at $2.60 a bushel.

In the gold market, bullion prices are likely to rise to $390 an ounce during the first half of next year and $400 in the second half, after establishing a floor at $360 on expected strong demand from Asia.
Gold prices recently fell to a three-year low of $366 an ounce.
Expectations of a correction in U.S. stock prices were also cited as a factor in the bullish gold forecast.
Lingering concerns about central bank gold sales ahead of European monetary union (EMU), however, will continue to cast a shadow over the bullion market in 1997, the report said.

Marubeni expects platinum prices to trend firmer to about $400 per ounce during the first half of next year and $420 in the second half, backed by increased demand from Asia's jewellery and autocatalyst sectors.
Selling from Russia, which helped pressure platinum prices late in 1996 to three-year lows around $366 an ounce, could fall next year as Russian platinum stocks are likely to dry up, the report said.
